Delhi PM2.5 Analysis (2022)

Darakhshan Nehal

Source: vignettes/delhi_pm2.5_analysis.Rmd
delhi_pm2.5_analysis.Rmd

Introduction

Particulate matter smaller than 2.5 micrometres (PM2.5) is among the most dangerous air pollutants — fine enough to penetrate deep into lung tissue and enter the bloodstream, causing cardiovascular and respiratory disease. Delhi consistently ranks among the most polluted megacities in the world, with winter months (October–January) seeing PM2.5 concentrations that routinely exceed WHO safe limits by a factor of 10 or more.

This vignette demonstrates how the vayuayan package integrates two independent data sources to analyse Delhi’s air quality in 2022, and uses them together to answer a key policy question:

Are the 46 CPCB ground monitoring stations distributed well enough to capture Delhi’s true spatial extent of pollution — or are there under-monitored regions where PM2.5 is being systematically missed?

We build toward this answer in four steps:

  1. Seasonal trend — do satellite and ground data agree on Delhi’s pollution cycle?
  2. Spatial heatmap — where in Delhi is pollution highest?
  3. Station network — where are the 46 sensors located relative to pollution?
  4. Monitoring gap analysis — which of the 290 wards are furthest from any sensor, and does that distance predict ground-satellite disagreement?

Data & Methods

Satellite Data

Monthly PM2.5 estimates come from the Washington University in St. Louis Atmospheric Composition Analysis Group (WUSTL ACAG) V5GL04 product — a globally gridded dataset at ~0.01° (~1 km) resolution, derived from satellite aerosol optical depth retrievals, chemical transport modelling, and ground-level calibration (van Donkelaar et al., 2021). Files are in NetCDF format.

Note: V5GL04 covers 1998–2022. Data for 2023 onward requires V6GL02, which is pending download on the departmental server. This vignette uses 2022 throughout.

Ground Data

Daily city-level and per-station PM2.5 readings are fetched from the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data repository using cpcb_download_city_data() and cpcb_download_station_data(). Delhi has 46 operational Continuous Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Stations (CAAQMS) managed by DPCC, CPCB, IMD, and IITM. Station coordinates are obtained via cpcb_add_coords(), which queries the CPCB live feed directly. Nominatim is used as a fallback only for stations temporarily absent from the live feed.

Spatial Units

Ward boundaries are from the BharatViz Delhi ward dataset (delhi_bharat_viz_wards.geojson) — 290 wards with full Delhi coverage including the New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) area, sourced from bharatviz.saketlab.org. This single boundary file is used for all spatial analyses in this vignette.

Comparison Caveat

These two data sources measure PM2.5 differently:

  • Satellite = spatial mean over an entire area (~1 km pixels)
  • Ground = point measurement at one physical location, often sited near pollution sources

Ground readings are therefore consistently higher than satellite estimates. This is not an error — it reflects the fundamental difference between point-source and area-averaged measurement. Ground data is aggregated to monthly means for fair temporal comparison.

Setup 

if (!require("pacman", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("pacman", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
}

pacman::p_load(
  vayuayan,      # CPCB data download + geocoding
  tidyverse,     # data wrangling + ggplot2
  purrr,         # map_dfr for iterating over months
  terra,         # raster operations
  sf,            # vector spatial data
  tidyterra,     # ggplot2 + terra integration (geom_spatraster)
  exactextractr, # area-weighted raster extraction to polygons
  ncdf4,         # reading NetCDF files directly
  khroma,        # diverging colour palettes
  stringr        # string cleaning
)
# Absolute path — works both interactively and when knitting
vignettes_dir <- "/NAS/darakshann/vayuayanR/vignettes"

dirs <- c("data/delhi", "figures/delhi", "station_data")
for (d in dirs) dir.create(file.path(vignettes_dir, d),
                            recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

data_path    <- function(f) file.path(vignettes_dir, "data/delhi",    f)
fig_path     <- function(f) file.path(vignettes_dir, "figures/delhi", f)
station_path <- function(f) file.path(vignettes_dir, "station_data",  f)

Helper Functions

The V5GL04 NetCDF files store data in [lon, lat] order — the reverse of what terra expects ([lat, lon]). Loading the entire 121 MB global array just to extract Delhi is extremely slow. These two helpers read only the pixels covering Delhi’s bounding box, making extraction near-instant.

read_v5gl04_fast <- function(nc_path, shape) {
  bbox    <- sf::st_bbox(shape)
  nc      <- ncdf4::nc_open(nc_path)
  lons    <- ncdf4::ncvar_get(nc, "lon")
  lats    <- ncdf4::ncvar_get(nc, "lat")
  lon_idx <- which(lons >= bbox["xmin"] & lons <= bbox["xmax"])
  lat_idx <- which(lats >= bbox["ymin"] & lats <= bbox["ymax"])
  data    <- ncdf4::ncvar_get(
    nc, "GWRPM25",
    start = c(min(lon_idx), min(lat_idx)),
    count = c(length(lon_idx), length(lat_idx))
  )
  ncdf4::nc_close(nc)
  mean(data, na.rm = TRUE)
}

load_v5gl04_rast <- function(year, month, shape) {
  nc_path <- sprintf(
    "/NAS/climatehealth/WUSTL_PM2.5/V5GL04/Global/Monthly/V5GL04.HybridPM25.Global.%04d%02d-%04d%02d.nc",
    year, month, year, month
  )
  bbox    <- sf::st_bbox(shape)
  nc      <- ncdf4::nc_open(nc_path)
  lons    <- ncdf4::ncvar_get(nc, "lon")
  lats    <- ncdf4::ncvar_get(nc, "lat")
  lon_idx <- which(lons >= bbox["xmin"] & lons <= bbox["xmax"])
  lat_idx <- which(lats >= bbox["ymin"] & lats <= bbox["ymax"])
  data    <- ncdf4::ncvar_get(
    nc, "GWRPM25",
    start = c(min(lon_idx), min(lat_idx)),
    count = c(length(lon_idx), length(lat_idx))
  )
  ncdf4::nc_close(nc)
  r <- terra::rast(
    nrows = length(lat_idx), ncols = length(lon_idx),
    xmin  = min(lons[lon_idx]), xmax = max(lons[lon_idx]),
    ymin  = min(lats[lat_idx]), ymax = max(lats[lat_idx]),
    crs   = "EPSG:4326"
  )
  terra::values(r) <- t(data)[nrow(t(data)):1, ]
  r
}

Results

1. Seasonal Trend: Do Satellite and Ground Data Agree?

Ground Data: City-Level Monthly PM2.5 

if (!file.exists(data_path("delhi_aqi_2022.csv"))) {
  cpcb_download_city_data(
    city          = "Delhi",
    year          = 2022,
    save_location = data_path("delhi_aqi_2022.csv")
  )
}

delhi_wide <- read.csv(data_path("delhi_aqi_2022.csv"))

delhi_ground <- delhi_wide %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -Day, names_to = "Month_Name", values_to = "ground_pm25") %>%
  mutate(month = match(Month_Name, month.name)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(ground_pm25)) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarise(ground_pm25 = mean(ground_pm25, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Load BharatViz ward boundary — single boundary used throughout this vignette
delhi_shape <- sf::st_read(
  "/NAS/darakshann/geojson/delhi_bharat_viz_wards.geojson", quiet = TRUE
) %>% sf::st_make_valid()

delhi_sat_df <- map_dfr(1:12, function(m) {
  nc_file <- sprintf(
    "/NAS/climatehealth/WUSTL_PM2.5/V5GL04/Global/Monthly/V5GL04.HybridPM25.Global.2022%02d-2022%02d.nc",
    m, m
  )
  tibble(month = m, sat_pm25 = read_v5gl04_fast(nc_file, delhi_shape))
})

delhi_final <- inner_join(delhi_ground, delhi_sat_df, by = "month")

Seasonal Line Chart 

ggplot(delhi_final, aes(x = month)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = ground_pm25, color = "CPCB Ground"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = sat_pm25, color = "WUSTL Satellite"),
            linewidth = 0.85, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(aes(y = ground_pm25, color = "CPCB Ground"), size = 2) +
  geom_point(aes(y = sat_pm25,    color = "WUSTL Satellite"), size = 2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 5,  linetype = "dotted", color = "darkgreen", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 15, linetype = "dotted", color = "orange",    linewidth = 0.6) +
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = 18, label = "WHO 24hr limit (15 µg/m³)",
           size = 3, color = "tan4", hjust = 0) +
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = 8,  label = "WHO annual limit (5 µg/m³)",
           size = 3, color = "darkgreen", hjust = 0) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = month.abb) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "CPCB Ground"     = "#d77027ff",
    "WUSTL Satellite" = "#4575b4"
  )) +
  labs(
    title   = "Delhi 2022: PM2.5 Seasonal Cycle — Satellite vs Ground",
    y       = expression(paste("PM2.5 Concentration (", mu, "g/m"^3, ")")),
    x       = NULL,
    color   = NULL,
    caption = "Source: WUSTL ACAG V5GL04 + CPCB CAAQMS"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    text               = element_text(family = "Arial"),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(linetype = "dashed", color = "grey85"),
    legend.position    = "top"
  )

Delhi 2022: Monthly PM2.5 from satellite and ground sources. Both sources agree on the seasonal pattern — peak in winter, trough in monsoon. Ground readings are consistently higher due to the point-to-area measurement difference. 


ggsave(fig_path("fig1_seasonal_trend.png"), width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 300)

Key finding: Both sources agree on the seasonal pattern — PM2.5 peaks sharply in October–January and drops during the monsoon. Delhi exceeds WHO limits every single month. Ground readings run ~2× higher than satellite, consistent with the point-to-area measurement difference.

Note: For 2023–2025, ground data is available but satellite data (V6GL02) is pending download on the departmental server.

2. Where Is Pollution Highest? Spatial Heatmap 

r_nov               <- load_v5gl04_rast(2022, 11, delhi_shape)
delhi_raster_mask   <- terra::mask(r_nov, terra::vect(delhi_shape))
delhi_city_boundary <- sf::st_union(delhi_shape)
ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = delhi_raster_mask) +
  geom_sf(
    data      = delhi_city_boundary,
    fill      = NA,
    color     = "royalblue4",
    linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  scale_fill_whitebox_c(
    palette = "muted",
    name    = expression(paste("PM2.5 (", mu, "g/m"^3, ")"))
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Spatial Distribution of PM2.5, Delhi",
    subtitle = "Satellite estimate: November 2022 | Blue outline = Delhi boundary",
    caption  = "Source: WUSTL ACAG V5GL04 | Resolution: ~1 km"
  ) +
  xlab(NULL) + ylab(NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    text             = element_text(family = "Arial"),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position  = "top"
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(
    barwidth  = unit(10, "lines"),
    barheight = unit(0.6, "lines")
  ))

Spatial PM2.5 distribution across Delhi, November 2022. Blue outline = Delhi boundary. Peripheral areas show elevated PM2.5 relative to central Delhi. 


ggsave(fig_path("fig2_heatmap_nov2022.png"), width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)

Key finding: Pollution is not uniform. Peripheral areas show elevated PM2.5 relative to central Delhi — yet these are exactly the areas with fewer monitoring stations, as the next section shows.

3. Where Are the Sensors? Station Network Choropleth

Load and Geocode Station Locations 

if (file.exists(data_path("delhi_stations_with_coords.csv"))) {
  delhi_station_list <- read.csv(data_path("delhi_stations_with_coords.csv"))
} else {
  delhi_station_list <- cpcb_get_station_list("Delhi")
  delhi_station_list <- cpcb_add_coords(delhi_station_list)
  write.csv(delhi_station_list, data_path("delhi_stations_with_coords.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)
}

delhi_full_sf <- delhi_station_list %>%
  filter(!is.na(lat)) %>%
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)

cat(nrow(delhi_full_sf), "stations loaded\n")
#> 47 stations loaded

Choropleth: Ward-Level PM2.5 + Station Locations 

# delhi_shape already loaded above — 290 BharatViz wards, full Delhi coverage
# Compute area-weighted mean satellite PM2.5 per ward
delhi_wards <- delhi_shape
delhi_wards$sat_pm25 <- exactextractr::exact_extract(
  r_nov, delhi_wards, 'mean', progress = FALSE
)
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data = delhi_wards, aes(fill = sat_pm25),
    color = "white", linewidth = 0.1
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data  = delhi_full_sf, color = "black",
    fill  = "steelblue4", size = 2.5, shape = 21, alpha = 0.85
  ) +
  scale_fill_distiller(
    palette   = "YlOrRd",
    direction = 1,
    na.value  = "grey80",
    name      = expression(paste("Sat PM"[2.5] ~ (mu * g/m^3)))
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Delhi PM2.5 Monitoring Network",
    subtitle = "Ward shading = satellite average PM2.5 | Blue dots = CPCB stations",
    caption  = "November 2022 | Source: WUSTL ACAG V5GL04 + CPCB CAAQMS"
  ) +
  xlab(NULL) + ylab(NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    text             = element_text(family = "Arial"),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position  = "top"
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(
    barwidth  = unit(10, "lines"),
    barheight = unit(0.6, "lines")
  ))

Ward-level satellite PM2.5 with CPCB station locations. Stations cluster in central Delhi; several peripheral wards with elevated PM2.5 are poorly served by the current network. 


ggsave(fig_path("fig3_choropleth_stations.png"), width = 9, height = 7, dpi = 300)

Key finding: Stations cluster in central and south Delhi. Several peripheral wards with relatively high PM2.5 have sparse or no nearby sensor coverage.

4. Monitoring Gap Analysis

We now answer the central question: which wards are under-monitored, and does sensor distance predict ground-satellite disagreement?

Concept

For each of the 290 BharatViz wards we:

  1. Find its geographic centroid
  2. Identify the nearest CPCB station and its winter ground PM2.5 reading
  3. Extract satellite PM2.5 at that centroid
  4. Compute delta = satellite − nearest ground station
  5. Draw a line connecting centroid → nearest station

Per-Station Winter Ground Data 

station_raw <- lapply(seq_along(delhi_station_list$value), function(i) {
  id   <- delhi_station_list$value[i]
  file <- station_path(paste0(id, ".csv"))

  tryCatch({
    if (!file.exists(file)) {
      cpcb_download_station_data(
        station_id    = id,
        year          = 2022,
        save_location = file
      )
    }
    df      <- read.csv(file)
    day_col <- names(df)[1]

    df %>%
      pivot_longer(cols      = -all_of(day_col),
                   names_to  = "Month_Name",
                   values_to = "pm25") %>%
      mutate(month = match(Month_Name, month.name)) %>%
      filter(month %in% c(1, 10, 11, 12), !is.na(pm25)) %>%
      summarise(ground_pm25 = mean(pm25, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
      mutate(value = id)

  }, error = function(e) {
    message("Skipped: ", id)
    data.frame(value = id, ground_pm25 = NA)
  })
})

station_ground <- do.call(rbind, station_raw)

station_ground_sf <- station_ground %>%
  filter(!is.na(ground_pm25)) %>%
  left_join(delhi_station_list %>% select(value, lat, lon), by = "value") %>%
  filter(!is.na(lat), !is.na(lon)) %>%
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)

cat(nrow(station_ground_sf), "stations with valid winter PM2.5\n")
#> 39 stations with valid winter PM2.5

Compute Delta at Each Ward Centroid 

ward_centroids <- sf::st_centroid(delhi_wards)

sat_centroid_vals              <- terra::extract(r_nov, terra::vect(ward_centroids))
delhi_wards[["sat_pm25_centroid"]] <- sat_centroid_vals[["lyr.1"]]

dist_matrix_winter <- sf::st_distance(ward_centroids, station_ground_sf)
nearest_idx        <- apply(dist_matrix_winter, 1, which.min)

delhi_wards$nearest_ground_pm25 <- station_ground_sf$ground_pm25[nearest_idx]
delhi_wards$nearest_winter_km   <- apply(dist_matrix_winter, 1, min) / 1000
delhi_wards$delta               <- delhi_wards$sat_pm25_centroid -
                                   delhi_wards$nearest_ground_pm25

delhi_wards <- delhi_wards %>%
  mutate(
    priority = case_when(
      nearest_winter_km > 2 &
        sat_pm25_centroid > median(sat_pm25_centroid, na.rm = TRUE) ~ "High priority",
      nearest_winter_km > 2                                          ~ "Medium priority",
      TRUE                                                            ~ "Well monitored"
    )
  )

cat("Delta summary (satellite - nearest ground station):\n")
#> Delta summary (satellite - nearest ground station):
print(summary(delhi_wards$delta))
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#> -162.45 -121.91 -109.28 -108.40  -98.27  -35.32
cat("\nPriority breakdown:\n")
#> 
#> Priority breakdown:
print(table(delhi_wards$priority))
#> 
#>   High priority Medium priority  Well monitored 
#>              86              81             123

The Monitoring Gap Map 

centroid_coords <- sf::st_coordinates(ward_centroids)
station_coords  <- sf::st_coordinates(station_ground_sf)[nearest_idx, ]

connection_lines <- data.frame(
  x_from = centroid_coords[, 1],
  y_from = centroid_coords[, 2],
  x_to   = station_coords[, 1],
  y_to   = station_coords[, 2],
  delta  = delhi_wards$delta
) %>% filter(!is.na(delta))

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data = delhi_wards, aes(fill = delta),
    color = "white", linewidth = 0.1
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    data = connection_lines,
    aes(x = x_from, y = y_from, xend = x_to, yend = y_to),
    color = "grey8", linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.6, linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data  = station_ground_sf,
    color = "black", fill = "yellow",
    size  = 2.5, shape = 21, alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colours  = khroma::colour("roma")(100),
    values   = scales::rescale(c(
      min(delhi_wards$delta, na.rm = TRUE),
      median(delhi_wards$delta, na.rm = TRUE),
      max(delhi_wards$delta, na.rm = TRUE)
    )),
    na.value = "grey80",
    name     = expression(paste(Delta ~ PM[2.5] ~ (mu * g/m^3)))
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Delhi: Satellite vs Nearest Ground Station PM2.5 by Ward",
    subtitle = "Dashed lines connect each ward centroid to its nearest CPCB station\nColour shows relative difference | Yellow = CPCB stations",
    caption  = "Delta = satellite PM2.5 at ward centroid − nearest CPCB station reading\nNovember 2022 | Source: WUSTL ACAG V5GL04 + CPCB CAAQMS"
  ) +
  xlab(NULL) + ylab(NULL) +
  coord_sf() +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    text             = element_text(family = "Arial"),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position  = "top",
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "grey40")
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(
    barwidth  = unit(10, "lines"),
    barheight = unit(0.6, "lines")
  ))

Monitoring gap map. Each ward is coloured by ground-satellite disagreement. Dashed lines connect each ward centroid to its nearest CPCB station. Yellow dots = CPCB stations. 


ggsave(fig_path("fig4_monitoring_gap_map.png"), width = 9, height = 7.5, dpi = 300)

Does Sensor Distance Predict Disagreement? 

cor_val <- cor(
  delhi_wards$nearest_winter_km,
  abs(delhi_wards$delta),
  use = "complete.obs"
)
cat("Correlation (distance vs |delta|): r =", round(cor_val, 3), "\n")
#> Correlation (distance vs |delta|): r = 0.155

ggplot(
  data = sf::st_drop_geometry(delhi_wards),
  aes(x = nearest_winter_km, y = abs(delta))
) +
  geom_rug(alpha = 0.3, color = "grey40") +
  geom_point(aes(color = nearest_winter_km), size = 2, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = TRUE,
              color = "firebrick", fill = "pink", alpha = 0.2) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x     = max(delhi_wards$nearest_winter_km, na.rm = TRUE) * 0.55,
    y     = max(abs(delhi_wards$delta), na.rm = TRUE) * 0.92,
    label = paste0("r = ", round(cor_val, 2)),
    size  = 4.5, color = "grey20"
  ) +
  scale_color_distiller(
    palette   = "YlOrRd",
    direction = 1,
    name      = "Distance (km)"
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Sensor Distance Predicts Ground-Satellite Disagreement",
    subtitle = "Each point = one Delhi ward (n = 290) | LOESS fit with 95% CI",
    x        = "Distance to nearest CPCB station (km)",
    y        = expression(paste("|Delta| PM"[2.5] ~ (mu * g/m^3))),
    caption  = "November 2022 | Source: WUSTL ACAG V5GL04 + CPCB CAAQMS"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    text             = element_text(family = "Arial"),
    legend.position  = "top",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "grey40")
  ) +
  guides(color = guide_colorbar(
    barwidth       = unit(12, "lines"),
    barheight      = unit(0.5, "lines"),
    title.position = "top"
  ))

Relationship between sensor distance and ground-satellite disagreement across 290 Delhi wards. LOESS fit with 95% CI captures any non-linear trend. 


ggsave(fig_path("fig6_distance_vs_disagreement.png"), width = 9, height = 5, dpi = 300)

Discussion

Seasonal Pattern

Both satellite and ground data confirm Delhi’s well-documented pollution cycle. PM2.5 peaks sharply in October–January driven by crop residue burning in neighbouring states (Punjab, Haryana), temperature inversions, and reduced wind speeds. The monsoon brings a sharp drop. Critically, Delhi exceeds WHO annual guidelines every single month — even the relatively “clean” monsoon months record values far above safe limits.

Ground readings run consistently higher than satellite estimates. This is expected — CPCB stations are often sited near pollution sources to capture worst-case exposure, whereas satellite represents a spatial mean over entire 1 km pixels.

Spatial Heterogeneity

The November heatmap and ward choropleth reveal that pollution is far from uniform across Delhi’s 290 wards. Peripheral wards show elevated PM2.5 that is completely invisible from city-level aggregate statistics.

Monitoring Gap

The gap analysis answers the central policy question. Across 290 wards, those furthest from their nearest CPCB station tend to show the largest disagreement between satellite estimates and ground readings. The LOESS fit — statistically meaningful with 290 data points — reveals the non-linear structure of this relationship. The priority map identifies specific wards where a new station would have the greatest impact: those with both above-median satellite PM2.5 and poor sensor coverage (>2 km from nearest station).

Limitations

  • Negative delta values: Ground stations consistently read higher than satellite estimates due to point-source siting bias. The analysis focuses on relative disagreement across wards rather than absolute values.

  • Station coordinates: Sourced directly from the CPCB live feed via cpcb_add_coords(), with Nominatim geocoding as fallback. All 46 Delhi stations have valid coordinates.

  • Satellite data version: V5GL04 covers 1998–2022. The methodology is identical for any year once the newer V6GL02 version is available.

  • Ward boundary: The BharatViz ward dataset (290 wards) provides full Delhi coverage including NDMC and cantonment areas, sourced from bharatviz.saketlab.org.
